about.title: About Protein Calculator - Daily Protein Intake
about.description: The Protein Calculator estimates daily protein intake based on weight, activity level, and fitness goals. Protein needs vary based on age, body size, activity level, and goal. Use the result as a general nutrition reference rather than an individualized medical or diet recommendation.

howTo.title: How to Use the Protein Calculator

steps.title: Enter Your Weight
steps.description: Input your current body weight and select your preferred units (kg or lbs).

steps.title: Choose Activity Level
steps.description: Select your activity level from sedentary to very active based on your exercise routine.

steps.title: Select Fitness Goal
steps.description: Choose your primary goal: maintenance, muscle building, weight loss, or athletic performance.

steps.title: View Protein Requirement
steps.description: See an estimated daily protein target in grams and relative to body weight.

steps.title: Plan Your Meals
steps.description: Use the recommendation to plan meals and distribute protein throughout the day.

steps.title: Track Your Intake
steps.description: Monitor your daily protein consumption to meet your calculated target.

faq.q: How much protein do I need per day?
faq.a: General guideline ranges often fall between 0.8 and 2.2 grams per kilogram of body weight depending on activity level and goals. The calculator uses your inputs to estimate a reference range, but individual needs can vary.

faq.q: Can I get enough protein from plant sources?
faq.a: Yes, plant-based proteins like legumes, quinoa, nuts, seeds, and protein-rich grains can meet protein needs when consumed in adequate amounts and variety. Combining different plant proteins ensures complete amino acid profiles.

Many people spread protein intake across meals and snacks to make daily targets easier to reach. Exact timing and meal size preferences vary, so use the calculator as a planning reference rather than a strict rule.

faq.q: What happens if I eat too much protein?
faq.a: Very high protein intake may not be appropriate for everyone, especially for people with certain medical conditions. If you have kidney concerns or need individualized nutrition guidance, consult a qualified healthcare provider or dietitian.
